html:
{#- LS Foods — Sales Order. Laid out like the client's item build sheet ("SALES ORDER SCREEN"): a beef / hog share prints as its deposit line — e.g. "Quarter Beef Deposit 4 x $600" for a whole beef — because on the order the share IS priced at its fixed deposit (share_billing.py). The hanging-weight charge and processing come on the final invoice. Other items print with their case weight and price. Totals: Total - Paid (the order's Advance Paid) = Total Due. On a share order that is what is owed now; the share's hanging-weight balance and processing are not on the order and come on the final invoice. -#} {%- set view = order_view(doc) %} {#- Rounded total when rounding is on, as ERPNext bills it. #} {%- set order_total = doc.rounded_total or doc.grand_total %} {%- set total_due = order_total - (doc.advance_paid or 0) %}
